name: Ali ibn al-Jahm
bio: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Jahm, of the clan of Sama ibn Lu'ayy, was a poet of Baghdad, a contemporary of Abu Tammam and a close companion of the caliph al-Mutawakkil. The caliph later turned against him and banished him to Khurasan, where he stayed for some time. He was known for the tenderness of his verse, and the critic Ibn Sharaf al-Qayrawani singled out his poem on al-Rusafa as his love poem. He later moved to Aleppo and set out from there with a raiding party; horsemen of the tribe of Kalb attacked them, and he died of his wounds in 249 AH (863 CE).
